title: Inconsistent route-translator weight rounding caused rollout weight drift and delayed rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a staged model rollout on 2026-02-23, the route translation service (console -> runtime) applied a non-deterministic rounding rule when converting percentage weights into tokenized routing rules. The intended canary weight (5%) was translated to 30% in a subset of regions, causing an unexpected traffic surge to the canary variant. The surge exposed a performance regression in that model variant and triggered elevated 5xx rates and tail latency. Attempts to rollback were delayed because the rollout controller encountered a version-pinning race and the rollback path exercised an older translation path that re-applied the same incorrect conversion for a short window.
timeline:
2026-02-23T14:08Z - Canary rollout started via Console (release rollout-id: r-20260223-01).
2026-02-23T14:12Z - Monitoring alerts: per-route tail latency > 2s in eu-west-1 and increased 5xx rate.
2026-02-23T14:14Z - First on-call triage: rollback requested.
2026-02-23T14:17Z - Rollback triggered via Console (manual rollback).
2026-02-23T14:19Z - Partial rollback completed in us-east-1; eu-west-1 remained at elevated canary weight.
2026-02-23T14:24Z - Investigation found route-translator produced weight mapping 5% -> 30% due to integer-rounding bug when converting floating percentage to integer-based shard routing config.
2026-02-23T14:36Z - Rollout controller race discovered: concurrent reconciliations applied an older, cached translation for a brief window, re-introducing the incorrect weight during the rollback.
2026-02-23T14:45Z - Engineers disabled automated rollouts for the affected project and applied an emergency hotfix to route-translator.
2026-02-23T15:02Z - All regions confirmed at intended weights and traffic stabilized.
2026-02-24 - Post-incident triage and stakeholder update prepared.
root_cause: Two independent but compounding defects: (1) route-translator's conversion logic used a floor/round-to-nearest heuristic that, for percentages under 10% and low shard counts, produced disproportionately large integer weights (example: 5% -> 1/3 -> ~33%). This was not covered by unit tests for low-percentage rollouts. (2) rollout controller caching/reconciliation timing race allowed an old translation to be reapplied during the rollback, preventing a clean revert until the cache TTL expired or the controller performed another reconciliation. The combination produced a transient but material traffic misallocation.
mitigation_taken:
- Immediate: Disabled automated rollouts for all model projects for 40 minutes; manual verification enforced for all rollbacks.
- Hotfix: Patch deployed to route-translator to use a deterministic rounding policy (bankers rounding with explicit minimum bucket size) and to emit a warning metric when the translated weight deviates from requested weight by >2%. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-translator/pull/1829)
- Rollout controller: Temporarily increased reconciliation frequency and cleared caches for active controllers in affected regions.
- Communication: Customer-facing incident summary sent to affected customers and internal postmortem shared with Sales/CS and Product.
impact_metrics:
Peak increased canary traffic in eu-west-1: +25 percentage points (intended 5% -> observed 30%).
Elevated 5xx rate: 1.8% -> 6.5% for the affected route during the incident window.
P95 latency: 450ms -> 1.9s.
Duration of elevated error/latency: ~40 minutes.
Number of customers with visible degradation: 7 (self-reported), scoped to routes using the affected model family.
actions: A1: Shipping deterministic rounding in route-translator and adding property-based tests for percentages 0.1% - 100% across all shard counts. Owner: Diego Alvarez. ETA: 2026-03-10.

A2: Add an invariant in the rollout controller: after applying a translate step, assert translated_weight within +/-2% of requested; if violated, abort rollout and open an alert. Owner: Priya Rao. ETA: 2026-03-05.
A3: Improve controller caching semantics to use versioned keys and conditional writes to prevent stale translations from overwriting recent reconciliations. Owner: Samuel Ortiz. ETA: 2026-03-18.

A4: Update runbook: require automated safety checks (translation sanity + traffic shadowing with 1000-request sample) before enabling >1% canary in production. Owner: On-call Platform Guild. ETA: 2026-03-08.
A5: Add an alerting rule that triggers when actual per-variant traffic deviates from configured weight by >10 percentage points for 1 minute. Owner: Observability team (Elena Park). ETA: 2026-03-04.
A6: Retroactive audit of all rollouts in the previous 90 days to surface any near misses where translation produced >3% deviation. Owner: SRE rotation. ETA: 2026-03-20.
A7: Customer remediation contact: Outreach to 7 affected customers with credit and technical write-up. Owner: Customer Success (Liam Foster). ETA: 2026-03-06.
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Decision: Use deterministic rounding (bankers rounding) plus a minimum bucket floor for tiny percentages to avoid surprising large jumps in low-shard deployments. Tradeoff: slightly less fidelity on micro-percentage allocations in favor of predictable behavior.
- Decision: Add runtime safety guard that aborts rollout on translation mismatch; tradeoff is additional rollout latency for the sanity check but much higher safety.
- Decision: Not to revert rollout-controller cache entirely to synchronous writes due to performance impact; instead we will implement versioned conditional updates.
follow_up_notes:
- This incident highlights gaps in our translation test surface (we lack property tests across shard distributions).
- Console UX: surface 'translated weight preview' before saving rollout config so operators can catch significant deviations. (PM enhancement request: PM-587).
- Consider adding a simulated dry-run in a staging control plane that shows expected distribution across regions before canary activation.
- Verify similar translation logic in dedicated/private agents for parity.
